dimensions.assessment: Affects federal employees receiving compensation or benefits under the FECA program, as well as administrators at the Department of Labor, SSA, and HHS.
dimensions.evidence: Upon receiving a written request from the Secretary of Labor with respect to one or more employees... the Commissioner of Social Security shall make available

dimensions.assessment: Grants data access rights to program administrators to verify earnings and prevent improper payments without altering benefit eligibility rules.
dimensions.evidence: To improve compliance with the requirements under, and the integrity of, the FECA program, and to detect and prevent improper payments

dimensions.assessment: Aims to reduce improper payments in federal workers' compensation, provided at no cost to the Secretary of Labor for data transfers.
dimensions.evidence: at no cost to the Secretary; and in accordance with the manner, frequency, and form specified in the applicable memorandum of understanding

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Federal Employees' Compensation Act to establish new data-sharing mechanisms and interagency procedures.
dimensions.evidence: Subchapter I of chapter 81 of title 5, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following: Sec. 8153. Data access

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent data access authority and ongoing procedural requirements for federal workers' compensation administration.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by this section shall apply with respect to payments made under subchapter I of chapter 81 of title 5, United States Code, on or after the date of enactment of this Act.

importance_detail.rationale: The bill amends the Federal Employees' Compensation Act to permit the Secretary of Labor to obtain earnings and employment data from the Social Security Administration and HHS without employee authorization to detect improper payments.
